Dataset

The following code will download a zip file with a dataset (and some other do files), unzip it and then remove everything but the data file

copy "https://www.stata-press.com/data/heus/heus.zip"  heus.zip
qui unzipfile heus.zip,replace
local datafiles: dir "." files "heus_*.do"
foreach datafile of local datafiles {
        rm `datafile'
}
rm heus.zip
ls heus*.dta

Problem

use "heus_mepssample",clear
drop if exp_tot == . | exp_tot == 0

regress exp_tot age##age i.female i.race_bl i.race_oth i.eth_hisp famsize ///
    i.ed_hs i.ed_hsplus i.ed_col i.ed_colplus lninc ///
    i.reg_midw i.reg_south i.reg_west i.anylim mcs12 pcs12 ///
    i.ins_mcare i.ins_mcaid i.ins_unins ins_dent
    
predict exp_hat

scatter exp_hat exp_tot, saving(pred_obs,replace) scheme(burd) ///
  xscale(log) xlabel(100 500 1500 5000 20000 80000) xline(1500 5000, ///
  lstyle(yxline)) yline(1500 5000, lstyle(yxline)) mcolor(%30) ///
  yline(0,lstyle(foreground)) xscale(lstyle(none)) ///
  xtitle("Total medical care expenditures (log scale)")  ///
  text(1500 80000 "Median", place(n)) text( 5000 80000 "Mean", place(n))

Graph of predicted expenditures vs observed

Another Problem

qui predict u, residual
twoway kdensity exp_tot if exp_tot<100000, scheme(burd) ///
    ytitle(density) xtitle(total expenditure) name(a, replace) nodraw
twoway  kdensity u if exp_tot<100000, scheme(burd) ///
    ytitle(density) xtitle(OLS residuals) name(b, replace) nodraw

What is GLM? - generalization of linear regression

\[\color{blue}{\text{For OLS: }}Y_i = \underbrace{\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} + \ldots}_\text{linear predictor } + \underbrace{ \epsilon_i}_\text{random part} \]

Which says:

  1. Y has a linear predictor part that is a sum of the regressors
  2. the linear predictor is the expected mean of Y or \(\mu\) (in this case)
  3. Y has a random component with a normal distribution
    \(\Rightarrow\) Y is normally distributed conditional on the regressors.

Or another way of presenting it \[ \mu_i=\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} + \ldots\] \[Y \sim N(\mu_i,\sigma)\]

Expand to a broader set of regressions

  1. An index composed of the sum of the regressors \[\eta_i = \underbrace{\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} + \ldots}_\text{linear predictor } \]

  2. A link function \(g(.)\) that linearizes the relationships of the covariates to the mean (and an inverse \(g(.)^{-1}\) that can reverse the process) \[\mu_i=g^{-1}(\eta_i)\]

  3. A random component supplied by an error generating function \[Y_i \sim \underbrace{f_y(y \mid \mu_i)}_{\text{pdf conditional on }\mu_i}\] pdf=probability distribution function (see biostats II section on PDFs )

OLS as the base case in the GLM framework

  1. A linear predictor: \(\eta_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} + \ldots\)
  2. Link is the Identify function \(g(x)=x=g^{-1}(x)\) )
  3. normal distribution function

So \[ \eta_i=\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} + \ldots\] \[\mu_i=\eta_i=g^{-1}(\eta_i)\] \[Y_i \thicksim N(\mu_i,\sigma) \Rightarrow Var(Y_i \mid \mu_i)=\sigma^2\]

Why do we need it?

Some response variables ( Y ) can not be generated or well described by a linear equation combined with a normally distributed function for the error term.

  • Like dichotomous data, ordinal data, categorical data or non-negative dependent variables (like count data)

  • Or any data where the variance changes with the mean (e.g like costs where there is more variability when the mean is larger)

GLM using the glm command in stata

Special purpose command GLM command
regress glm <vars>, family(gaussian) link(identity)
logit,logistic glm <vars>, family(binomial) link(logit)
probit glm <vars>, family(binomial) link(probit)
poisson glm <vars>, fam(poisson) link(log)
nbreg glm <vars>, fam(nbinomial ml) link(log)
  • In most cases do not need to use glm because there are all of the special purpose commands which work more efficiently and which add other bells and whistles.

Logistic regression GLM

  1. A linear predictor: \(\eta_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} + \ldots\)
  2. Link for \(\mu_i(=p_i)\) is the logit function \(g(p_i)=\ln \frac{p_i}{1-p_i}\)
  3. Binomial distribution function

So \[ \begin{align} \color{blue}{\eta_i} & =\color{blue}{\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} + \ldots} \\ Pr(Y=1)=p_i=\color{blue}{\mu_i} &= \color{blue}{g^{-1}(\eta_i)}= \frac{1}{1+e^{-\eta_i}}=\frac{1}{1+e^{-(\beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} + \ldots)}} \\ \color{blue}{Y_i} &\thicksim \color{blue}{Binom(p_i,n_i)} \Rightarrow Var(Y \mid p_i)=p_i(1-p_i) \\ \end{align}\]
